inventory.description: Pure, host-testable modules (Packages/VisualCore): Math, Simulation (SceneClock, FixedStepClock, SeededRandom, AccessibilityPreferences), Scenes (PointerTracker, ExportGeometry), ShaderSource, EffectsGraph, Diagnostics (FramePacing), Parameters, Persistence, TestSupport (+ placeholder AudioDSP). iOS modules (Packages/VisualCoreRendering): Rendering, Effects, UI, Automation (Debug/measurement) (+ placeholder Audio). Rules R1-R5 enforced by scripts/check_dependencies.py.

RenderHost owns the EGL display/context/surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend, a CAMetalLayer RenderView, a frame scheduler and context generations. All GL work runs on the main thread (@MainActor; dispatchPrecondition in DEBUG). pause/resume, recreateContext (context loss) and destroy; scenes implement RenderScene setup/resize/render/teardown.

ResourceRegistry creates textures, buffers, render targets and programs under a ResourceBudget, pools render targets, caches programs, counts leaks and rejects stale handles after a generation change.

ShaderLibrary expands includes and defines with line maps; ResourceRegistry.program compiles/links through ANGLE and reports ShaderDiagnostic file:line; color-space policy in docs/rendering/color-space.md.
Versioned effect-graph description, validator (≤ 32 passes, memory quota) and GPU executor with 8 pass types; EffectScene wraps any scene and adds the Reduce Flashing limiter.

Pointer tracking and tap/drag/pinch/rotate recognizers, scene graph and mesh generators; fixed-step clock, seeded RNG, timelines/tweens and particle system; primitive/particle/mesh renderers and the UIKit touch adapter.

XcodeGen 2.46.0 specs (root project.yml for Showcase and app targets; harness specs), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, unsigned simulator builds, and scripts/release_check.py (53 steps at A04-P00, listed by --list; the count grows as apps add steps): shared checks (docs, compliance, dependencies, public API, licenses, script tests, contracts), per-app documented-API, isolation, host and simulator app steps, per-app release steps generated from docs/apps/<slug>/release.json, and the reference regression steps.
Reference pinned at d93edd1 (ADR-0005), read-only; baseline steps via scripts/run_reference_baseline.py, read-only check scripts/check_reference_clean.py, ProjectMReference harness tests.
Apps own product composition, content and one-off rules (Apps/<Name>/); VisualCore owns reusable logic (constitution 1.2.0 Principle II 'Maximize reuse'); ProjectM stays in the harness (R1).
VisualCoreTestSupport (test targets only): ImageComparison/ImageDifference/ImageStatistics for pixel tests (A01-P01).

RenderView turns UIKit touches into PointerEvents (id, phase, position in points); PointerTracker keeps active pointers; tap/drag/pinch recognizers in VisualCoreScenes. No per-pointer velocity or rate-capped resampling yet.

inventory.area: Frame pacing, thermal state and time
inventory.description: FramePacing derives max FPS and render scale from thermal state and Low Power Mode (applied by RenderHost's FrameScheduler); SceneClock (play/pause/scrub/rate), FixedStepClock (fixed simulation steps), SeededRandom (xoshiro256**).

RenderHost.renderOffscreen + StillImageEncoder (opaque sRGB PNG) + ExportGeometry (A01-P04); release tooling shared by every app: check_privacy_manifest.py, check_app_release.py, bundle_licenses.py, AutomationView, AcknowledgementsView (A01-P06). A02-P06 reuses the release tooling unchanged and adds VisualCorePersistence.TemporaryFolder (app-owned short-lived files, emptied at launch) for capture crash recovery.
Palette (sample, builtIns) and ParameterSchema in VisualCoreParameters; Tween/Timeline and SceneClock in VisualCoreSimulation; EasingCurve in VisualCoreMath.
Camera2D (pan/zoom/rotate in points, zoom clamped 0.1…100) and ViewMetrics (points↔pixels). No double-precision complex-plane viewport (gap G-VIEWPORT).
DocumentStore (versioned envelopes, atomic writes, migrations, per-file problems; A01 library) and TemporaryFolder (short-lived files emptied at launch; A02 captures).

ParticleSystem (VisualCoreSimulation): seeded, deterministic, fixed-capacity CPU simulation (default 10,000, cap 100,000; dropped emissions counted) with Emitter (point source, rate, lifetime, speed, direction cone, start/end size and color) and ParticleForce (gravity, drag, radius-bounded attractor); checksum() for replay; instances() for drawing. A01's ParticleReplay is the consumer.

ParticleRenderer (VisualCoreRendering): instanced soft-edged quads (vcglDrawArraysInstanced) from ParticleInstance arrays through a per-frame instance buffer in the ResourceRegistry; premultiplied 'over' blending only; rebuilt after context recreation. A01's ParticlesArtScene is the consumer.

PingPongTarget and FieldPass (VisualCoreRendering, A02): two textures swapped each pass and a fragment pass into a target — the basis for a decaying trail texture; FloatRenderSupport reports half-float support.

QualityPolicy (VisualCoreDiagnostics) picks a tier from thermal state and Low Power Mode with hysteresis; AccessibilityPreferences / SystemAccessibility (VisualCoreSimulation) carry Reduce Motion and Reduce Flashing. A02's PlaygroundModel uses both.
NamedLibrary (VisualCorePersistence, A03) on DocumentStore: named, favoritable documents with schema versions, damage reports and caller validation; A03's Bookmark is the consumer.

matrix.notes: Closed in A04-P01 (G-SIMSTEP): FixedStepRunner over the FixedStepSimulation protocol (ParticleSystem conforms) — fixed 1/120 s steps, at most 8 per frame with dropped time counted, pause/resume without catch-up, invalid frames counted, and a ControlStream applied by step index so replays match however frames are split; the committed replay fixture (replay-v1.json) is bit-exact on the macOS host and both simulators. The simulation stays on the CPU (no compute shaders on OpenGL ES through ANGLE, research R1); drawing moves to the GPU in Phase 02.
Per-frame instance upload into a registry-owned buffer, released and rebuilt with the context (research R2).
Only premultiplied 'over' blending exists; additive blending and a trail-decay pass are gap G-BLENDTRAIL (research R4).
Touch-to-force mapping is app content on these (research R5).

matrix.capability: Multiple emitter families with bounded particle counts
matrix.notes: Closed in A04-P01 (G-EMITTERS): EmitterShape point/line/ring, EmitterBurst, Emitter.radial and Emitter.clamped() in VisualCoreSimulation; a point draws no extra random number, so A01 and the baselines are unchanged. The app's four families (Fountain, Curtain, Halo, Firework) stay within the scene limit (100-20,000) with drops counted.

matrix.capability: Point attractors, repulsors and gravity/wind fields
matrix.notes: gravity, drag and a radius-bounded attractor exist; repulsors with falloff, wind and singularity-safe softening are gap G-FIELDS (research R7).

matrix.capability: Adjustable particle size, lifetime, color gradient and trail strength
matrix.notes: Size and lifetime ranges and start/end colors exist; multi-stop gradients map through Palette; trail strength depends on G-BLENDTRAIL (research R8).

matrix.capability: Pause, reseed and save a scene
matrix.notes: Seeded systems replay exactly (checksum); scenes persist as app content on NamedLibrary (G-PSCENE, research R9).
Tiers exist; a particle-count mapping per tier is gap G-PQUALITY (research R10). Reduce Flashing is available.

gaps.test: Host tests: the CPU particle simulation advances in fixed steps with capped substeps per frame and a bounded catch-up after a pause or background (no unbounded fast-forward); replaying a seed with the same controls and fixed-step stream reproduces position fixtures exactly (checksum)
gaps.justification: Found in A04-P00 (research R1): the OpenGL ES path has no compute shaders, so the 'GPU-oriented' simulation is a bounded CPU simulation drawn on the GPU; every particle or physics app (A09, A11, A19) needs the same deterministic stepping. GPU-side state stays a later idea.

gaps.test: Host tests: point, line, ring and burst emitter shapes spawn inside their shape with the seeded generator; totals never exceed the pool capacity and drops are counted; invalid parameters are clamped
gaps.justification: Found in A04-P00 (research R6): emitter shapes are generic particle machinery (A09 Digital Aquarium bubbles, A19 Living Wallpapers).

gaps.test: Host tests: repulsors, falloff attractors, wind and vortex fields produce finite accelerations for every position including exactly at the center (softened singularities, fixture 4); accelerations are bounded
gaps.justification: Found in A04-P00 (research R7): force fields are reused by physics and creature apps (A11, A09).

gaps.test: Host tests: a particle-budget mapping gives each QualityPolicy tier a count cap; a high requested count respects the configured cap and drops with the tier under heat or Low Power Mode (fixture 2)
gaps.justification: Found in A04-P00 (research R10): count-based quality is generic to any instanced workload.

gaps.test: Package tests on both runtimes: ParticleRenderer draws with an additive blend option; a trail-decay pass on PingPongTarget fades by a set factor per frame, and resizing or clearing the trail targets leaks no textures (fixture 3); reduced-flash mode caps brightness
gaps.justification: Found in A04-P00 (research R4): additive glow and decaying trails are generic effects for many apps (A10 Neon Arcade, A21 Aurora).

reasons: Every capability maps to existing VisualCore API (5 available: buffer management, instanced rendering, interaction parameters, size/lifetime/gradient, pause/reseed/save) or an additive gap (5 adaptation rows).

All gaps are additive and reusable: G-SIMSTEP and G-EMITTERS and G-FIELDS (VisualCoreSimulation), G-PQUALITY (VisualCoreDiagnostics), G-BLENDTRAIL (VisualCoreRendering); scene presets stay app content on NamedLibrary. None needs a second renderer, compute shaders, a fork, private API or networking.

The simulation stays on the CPU (deterministic, bounded) and only drawing uses the GPU, because the OpenGL ES path offers no compute shaders (research R1); counts are capped and tiered (risk 3), additive blending gets a reduced-flash cap (risk 2), and instanced drawing is already proven by A01 (risk 1).
Reference regression baseline recorded green 7/7 (T-A04-003) and the empty shell builds and passes its smoke test on both simulator runtimes (T-A04-005).
Phase 01 starts with G-SIMSTEP and G-EMITTERS in VisualCoreSimulation and the app's seeded scene model.

A04-P01: a seeded, GPU-free particle domain — four emitter families with bounded counts on VisualCore's new emitter shapes and bursts (G-EMITTERS), a versioned validated ParticleScene, and VisualCore's FixedStepRunner (G-SIMSTEP) with a committed replay fixture that is bit-exact on host and both simulators; the sandbox shows a CPU preview with live and dropped counts, play/pause/step and new seed.
